name: the gate is never armed
why: Stops _countLiveDateFlags() caching its 'no flags here' answer, so every filter pass walks every row again — the state PERFORMANCE.org Step 25 describes. Must fail on the gate test: the scan counter moves after a keystroke.

name: the gate is read but never honoured
why: Removes the early return, leaving the bookkeeping in place. Same observable as above and pinned by the same assertion; listed separately because the two halves can be broken independently — a refactor that keeps the flag but drops its use looks harmless in a diff.
grep: stops scanning after the first pass

name: the gate closes on a page that HAS flags
why: Caches 'no flags' unconditionally, ignoring what the tally found. The ⚠️ button then disappears on the first filter pass after the render — the same user-visible loss as AUDIT.md §3.6, reached from the opposite direction. This is the mutation that makes the guarantee test earn its place: without it, `return result` at the top of the function would pass the gate test.

name: building a flag no longer arms the 'present' signal
why: Drops the _appendLiveDateFlag() assignment. The tally over the captured rows still finds the flags and sets it true, so this is covered for — the assignment matters for the ORDER (a pass that runs before capture must not conclude 'none'), which no fixture reaches. KNOWN UNCOVERED, kept because it is the only signal that does not depend on the DOM.

name: a new fetch inherits the previous page's answer
why: Drops the reset in startFetchingProcess(). Each fixture spec loads one page and fetches once, so nothing here re-fetches with a different row set. KNOWN UNCOVERED; the reset is belt-and-braces anyway, since _appendLiveDateFlag() re-arms the signal on any page that builds one.

name: a hydrated snapshot inherits the previous answer
why: Drops the reset in _hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData(). Hydrated rows carry their flags as stored HTML without _appendLiveDateFlag() ever running, so a page that had concluded 'no flags' would keep both buttons hidden. No fixture spec drives Load-from-Disk into a flagged release, so this is KNOWN UNCOVERED — and it is the gate's sharpest edge, recorded here rather than left implicit.

name: the per-row scan loses the flag's own column
why: Pins the other half of the change: the column index now comes from the flag's <td> rather than from a per-cell loop. Hard-coding it makes every flag fall into one positional bucket. Must fail on the breakdown test.
